seoTitle: Use TradingView Paper Trading & Fix a Missing Panel
metaDescription: Learn how to enable TradingView Paper Trading, place buy and sell orders, set stop loss and take profit, and fix the panel when it's not visible.
intro: Practicing trades without risking real money is exactly what TradingView's Paper Trading is built for, but a lot of users run into trouble when the panel simply won't show up. This guide covers how to enable Paper Trading, place buy and sell orders, manage stop loss and take profit, and fix the common issue of the panel not appearing on screen. It's aimed at beginners and active traders practicing their strategies in 2026.

steps.heading: Enable Paper Trading
steps.body: Locate and activate the Paper Trading feature within TradingView to start practicing with simulated funds.

steps.heading: Place buy and sell orders
steps.body: Use the Paper Trading panel to place simulated buy and sell trades just as you would with a live account.

steps.heading: Manage stop loss and take profit
steps.body: Set stop loss and take profit levels on your simulated trades to practice proper risk management.

steps.heading: Fix the Paper Trading panel not being visible
steps.body: If the panel disappears, check your layout settings or try reopening the Paper Trading section from the main menu.

steps.heading: Reset your layout if the panel still won't show
steps.body: As a last resort, reset your chart layout to default, which often resolves display issues caused by conflicting panel settings.

faq.question: Why is my TradingView Paper Trading panel not showing up?
faq.answer: This is often caused by a layout or display setting conflict, and can usually be fixed by reopening the panel or resetting your layout.

faq.question: Can I set a stop loss on a Paper Trading order?
faq.answer: Yes, Paper Trading supports setting stop loss and take profit levels just like placing orders on a live trading account.

faq.question: Does Paper Trading use real market prices?
faq.answer: Yes, Paper Trading typically uses live or near real-time market prices while simulating trades with virtual funds instead of real money.

faq.question: Is Paper Trading free to use on TradingView?
faq.answer: Paper Trading access can depend on your account type, so check your specific plan for availability and any related feature limits.
